name: Long Put (standard directional)
summary: Buy one OTM-to-ATM put for leveraged downside with risk capped at the debit.
max_profit: (strike - underlying at exit) x 100 - debit; maximum when the underlying goes to zero

greeks.theta: negative, similar magnitude to the equivalent call
greeks.vega: positive - and puts benefit from volatility skew expanding during selloffs, a real structural tailwind

when_to_use: IVR < 40, price below a falling 20 EMA with the 20 below the 50, no earnings before exit. Puts tolerate slightly higher IVR than calls because downside moves usually expand IV further.
entry_rules: Price < 20 EMA and 20 EMA < 50 EMA on the daily
No earnings before the planned exit
Limit order at mid, walk down in $0.05 steps
management_rules: If VIX spikes above 30 and the position is profitable, take the profit - put vega gains mean-revert fast
exit_rules: Sell to close at +100%, -50%, or 21 DTE

Hard flatten by 15:30 ET on expiration day. An ITM long put auto-exercises into a SHORT 100-share position - an uncovered equity short the account cannot carry. This is the more dangerous of the two auto-exercise cases
Abandon contracts worth < $0.05 rather than paying to exit
assignment_risk: No assignment (long). Auto-exercise creates short stock, strictly worse than the call case. The 15:30 ET flatten is mandatory and must fire even when the put is only marginally ITM.
common_mistakes: Buying puts after the VIX has already spiked (buying vega at the top); letting an ITM put expire and waking up short 100 shares.
